applies_why: The text decides a collision between the defender's Isaiah 7:14 link and the challenger's own chain read together (its Link 6 press), the exact chain-against-chain situation the rule governs.
quote: the sign itself does not state the mechanism
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: The rule's phrase 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side': on one reading it retires using any row's own non-statement as a verdict's ground, so grounding UNDERDETERMINED in 'the sign itself does not state the mechanism' breaches; on the other it retires only using non-statement to confirm or defeat a link, and a neutral echo both chains concede would be clean; I weighed the first reading heavier because the clause stands as the verdict's operative stated ground and the text supplies no footing comparison between [CR2]'s 8:8 and 9:6-7 answer and [DR3]'s bounds press that could instead carry the verdict.
why: The judge leaves the chain-against-chain collision underdetermined on the ground that the sign row itself does not state the mechanism, which is the retired stating-verse test applied at the judge's seat rather than a weighing of the two chains by footing.
